claim: Barroso, Edelen & Karehnke's crowding model for momentum predicts tail risk only when arbitrageurs ignore feedback effects; when arbitrageurs rationally condition on feedback, crowding does not generate tail risk. Empirically, using institutional-holdings-based crowding proxies, they find a NEGATIVE relation between crowding and expected crash risk, casting theoretical and empirical doubt on crowding as a stand-alone source of tail risk.
stance_target: the general claim that factor/stock crowding mechanically produces higher crash risk
scope_conditions: US equities, momentum strategy, peer-reviewed JFQA 2022 (published online 2021)
quoted_support: crowding does not generate tail risk when arbitrageurs rationally condition on feedback. Consistent with rational demands, our empirical analysis generally finds a negative relation between crowding proxies constructed from institutional holdings and expected crash risk. Thus our analysis casts both theoretical and empirical doubt on crowding as a stand-alone source of tail risk.
entities: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
